supporting_observations.claim: There were two failed network logons for ben.carter using NTLM from 192.0.2.45, followed about three minutes later by a successful network logon for the same account from that same address using Kerberos.
On WS-BCARTER-01, explorer.exe set the user's ProxyEnable value to 0 at 13:39 UTC, shortly before the failed logons.

On WS-BCARTER-01, explorer.exe wrote UserAssist entries whose encoded paths correspond to Chrome before the authentication failures and Excel afterward; these records do not establish who initiated the authentication attempts.
The failed logons followed by a success and the nearby proxy-setting change warrant investigation, but the available records do not establish malicious intent or identify the source device or actor.

known_telemetry_limitations: Proxy logs for the proxy host were not collected from 13:30 through 14:10 UTC on 2026-10-20, overlapping the alerted activity.
The supplied authentication records identify the source as 192.0.2.45 but do not map that address to a device or user.
claims_not_established: Whether the authentication attempts originated from ben.carter's workstation or another device.
Whether the failed logons resulted from an ordinary password error, a stale credential, or an unauthorized attempt.
Whether the successful logon was authorized and what resource or activity followed it.
Whether setting ProxyEnable to 0 was intentional proxy bypass or a benign configuration change.
Whether any suspicious network activity occurred during the proxy logging outage.
additional_evidence_needed: Map 192.0.2.45 to a device and user using DHCP, address-management, network, or endpoint records for the relevant time.
Review the source endpoint's authentication and process telemetry, including any credential use and network connections around 13:40-13:45 UTC.
Obtain proxy logs if recoverable and review available network connection, DNS, and TLS records for the source and WS-BCARTER-01 during the alert window.
Confirm with ben.carter and review any relevant password or application changes to determine whether the failed attempts and subsequent success were expected.
